report:
**Conclusion: False.** There is no scientific evidence that drinking boiled garlic water cures or treats COVID-19. This claim is a debunked health myth that circulated widely on social media early in the pandemic.

Multiple fact-checking organizations investigated this claim as early as February 2020 and found no evidence supporting it. AFP Fact Check consulted health professionals who confirmed there was no evidence for garlic-based remedies as effective COVID-19 treatments (factcheck.afp.com). Similarly, Rappler's fact-check explicitly labeled claims that "heat, garlic, ginger" can prevent or cure COVID-19 as false, noting there is no official cure or preventive treatment for the disease (rappler.com).

The World Health Organization directly addressed this myth in its official COVID-19 "Mythbusters" resource, stating that while garlic has some antimicrobial properties, "there is no evidence from the current outbreak that eating garlic has protected people from the new coronavirus" (who.int).

Importantly, no legitimate clinical or virological evidence exists showing garlic—boiled, raw, or otherwise—has any antiviral effect against SARS-CoV-2 in humans. Claims promoting garlic water as a "cure" are misinformation, not supported by peer-reviewed research or health authorities.

**Bottom line:** Boiled garlic water does not cure COVID-19. This is a false claim rejected by the WHO and independent fact-checkers. Individuals should rely on evidence-based treatments and vaccines, and consult healthcare professionals rather than unproven home remedies.

**Sources:**

2. https://www.rappler.com/newsbreak/fact-check/264621-heat-garlic-ginger-cure-covid-19/
3. https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/advice-for-public/myth-busters
